newsitem.title: INDIA: India BSE asks brokers to hold Bank Baroda trades.
newsitem.headline: India BSE asks brokers to hold Bank Baroda trades.

text.p: The Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) on Friday asked brokers not to confirm transactions in shares of state-run Bank of Baroda to their clients.

"To enable the exchange management to take a final decision in respect of such transactions, the trading is suspended for the day. Members are requested not to confirm such transactions to their clients," BSE said in an announcement.
The exchange had earlier suspended the shares due to confusion arising from the simultaneous listing of its partly- and fully-paid shares.
A BSE source told Reuters the exchange may consider cancelling transactions in Bank of Baroda shares.
But he said no final decision had been taken.
In its initial public offer last December, Bank of Baroda issued 100 million shares of 10 rupees face value at 85 rupees a share.
For retail investors, employees and banks, Bank of Baroda collected 25 rupees on application and 25 rupees on allotment. The balance will be collected later in the year.
Shares issued to non-resident Indians, overseas corporate bodies and foreign institutional investors were fully-paid shares at 85 rupees each.
Brokers said early trade was confused as most investors were unsure which price quotes reflected the shares they held. Both shares listed at 35 rupee levels.
